Cold side light separates every chain and icy rod from red leather. Both gloves and all three rods remain in frame. Normal speed, short natural motion blur. Planted staggered feet and slight yielding of knees and elbows. Dante watches the returning rod with focused confidence. The hands perform the action; no jump, whole-body spin, camera orbit, cut, flash or slow motion.
0.00-2.20: RIGHT glove holds a solid baton as in <Video 1>. The wrist and forearm initiate an outward/downward circle. The other TWO rods respond after the impulse, their rigid bodies lagging behind and being pulled into visible free arcs by the central ring and taut branches. Follow their actual changing orientations in the guide: they rise outward, cross open air in front of the waist, and return. They do not merely remain vertical under a twirling held baton. Keep the weapon clearly in foreground air, separated from torso and coat. Elbow yields to absorb the return; rod lengths and attachment points remain constant.
2.20-2.80: Follow the guide's actual free-baton catch. LEFT palm approaches the returning cyan handle already connected to the central ring, visibly closes its fingers around that SOLID BATON and damps its movement. RIGHT fingers open and release the formerly held baton after the left grip closes. The receiving glove grasps the handle body, not links or ring. The third rod stays attached and continues moving outside both hands. No new baton appears inside a fist; the rod approaching the palm is the same object retained after contact.
2.80-8.00: LEFT hand now drives its captured baton as in <Video 1>. The formerly held RIGHT baton and original spare third baton are the TWO free rods. Follow their changing angles, weighted pendular arcs, chain tension and slack through the rest of the guide. They must react to the new driver's impulse rather than hanging in the old anchor pose. Let the working wrist reverse direction, the free rods trail and return, and the elbow yield again. RIGHT hand stays open clear of the working branches. Keep all three batons rigid, separate and continuously attached to their original central ring. Continue a real weighted arc through the final second, ending mid-flow. Hands, rods and chains never pass through the body, gloves or each other. No held-baton-only twirl, bundled rods or static ending.
